title: Immunofluorescence assay for demyelination, remyelination, and proliferation in an acute cuprizone mouse model
protocol: Fill the 1 mL tuberculin syringe with Tamoxifen and wipe the tip of the filled syringe with a kimwipe before attaching a 27G needle to the syringe.
Administer 250 μL/day (5 mg/day) of 20 mg/mL Tamoxifen by intraperitoneal injection to each mouse, on alternate days, for a total of 4 i.p. injections.
Scruff the mouse and insert the needle into the lower left or right quadrant of the abdomen, perpendicular to the surface of the skin.
Aspirate to check for the presence of fluid prior to injecting the drug.
Alternate between the left and right side for i.p. injections.
Do not aspirate fluid before injecting the drug.
If red blood is aspirated, remove and discard the needle properly.
Use a clean syringe to perform the i.p. injection again at a different site.
If clear or yellow urine is aspirated, watch for turbid white discharge from the urethra for about 2 days.
Inject Tamoxifen intraperitoneally at a dose of 20 mg per mouse.
Ensure that mice have weights ranging from 20 g to 60 g.
Change the diet to 0.2% cuprizone pellets one week after the last Tamoxifen injection.
Transfer the mice to a clean cage before starting the cuprizone diet.
Prevent the mice from eating any leftover regular chow buried in the bedding.
Provide the cuprizone diet and water ad libitum for 5 weeks.
Discard the pellets every 2–3 days and replenish with fresh cuprizone pellets.
Feed each mouse 3 g of cuprizone diet per day to avoid discarding excessive amounts of food.
Change the diet to regular chow after 5 weeks of cuprizone diet to allow for remyelination.
Store vacuum sealed bags of Cuprizone pellets at −20°C.
Refrigerate opened bag at 4°C, away from light and use within 4 weeks.
Provide 0.2% Cuprizone diet in powdered form by mixing 0.2 g of cuprizone with 99.8 g of powdered chow as an alternative to pellets.
Feed healthy control mice regular chow in the powdered form.
Place powdered diet in a feeding jar on the floor of the cage and change daily.
Prepare working solution of EdU at a concentration of 2.5 mg/mL.
Administer 20 μL of 2.5 mg/mL EdU per gram body weight of mouse by i.p. injection, or 50 mg/kg body weight in total.
Inject EdU 24 hours prior to euthanasia.
Set up the peristaltic pump.
Connect the scalp vein set tubing to the outlet tube of the peristaltic pump.
Insert one tube of the pump into a container with 1× PBS (30 mL/mouse).
Insert another tube into a container with 4% PFA solution (30 mL/mouse).
Attach the tubing from the two containers to a 3-way stopcock.
Set the pump speed at 8 mL/min.
Fill the main outlet line with 1× PBS until there is a steady stream without bubbles from the needle.
Turn off the peristaltic pump and turn the stopcock to allow the flow of 4% PFA.
Pump 4% PFA until the fluid has reached the stopcock but not entered the main line.
Turn off the peristaltic pump and turn the stopcock to allow the flow of 1× PBS.
Anesthetize the mouse by administering 120 mg/kg of Fatal Plus (390 mg/mL Pentobarbitol sodium) via i.p. injection using a tuberculin syringe with 27G needle.
Lay the mouse on its back on a cork board or flat piece of styrofoam placed in a dissecting tray after it is completely unresponsive to painful stimuli but the heart is still beating.
Pin all four limbs of the mouse to the cork board using dissection pins or needles.
Expose the heart.
Incise the skin over the abdomen and chest with a large forcep.
Dissect the diaphragm with small dissecting scissors, being careful not to puncture the beating heart.
Cut the ribcage on both sides of the sternum with a small scissor.
Lift the sternum with a forcep to expose the heart.
Pin the xiphoid process to the dissection board with a needle.
Make a nick in the right auricle using small pointed scissors.
Insert a butterfly needle connected to the peristaltic pump into the apex of the heart.
Turn on the peristaltic pump and perfuse with 30 mL of 1× PBS at approximately 8 mL/min.
Switch the stopcock to perfuse with 60 mL of 4% PFA at the same rate.
Remove bubbles from the main line by expelling them with the needle outside the heart.
Collect the brain after bubble removal and preparation of the solution for injection.
Remove the needle from the heart and the pins holding the mouse to the dissection board.
Cut the head at the base of the skull using large scissors (supercut surgical scissors).
Remove skin from the dorsal side of the head using a smaller pair of scissors (supercut iris scissor).
Insert the blade of a small scissor through the foramen magnum and cut the skull bone laterally up to the orbit on both sides, avoiding damage to the brain.
Make another midline incision through the skull bone along the sagittal suture, extending anteriorly past the eyes with a small scissor (supercut iris scissor).
Carefully remove the skull bone from around the brain using thin pointed forceps (Dumont forceps), starting by gently pulling the bone laterally away from the midline on either side.
Release the olfactory bulbs if necessary, ensuring they are no longer attached to the bone before removing the brain.
Separate the brain along with the olfactory bulbs from the skull using flat forceps.
Drop the separated brain into a 15 mL conical tube containing 5 mL of 4% PFA.
Incubate the brain in 4% PFA for 4–6 hours at 4°C.
Remove the brain from the 4% PFA solution and place it in a petri dish using flat forceps.
Drop the brain into a 15 mL conical tube containing 15 mL of 30% sucrose solution.
Incubate the brain in 30% sucrose solution at 4°C on a nutating mixer at 20–30 rpm for 12–16 hours.
Remove the brain from the sucrose solution by gently emptying the tube into a petri dish.
Roll the brain on a lint-free paper napkin like kimwipe to remove excess sucrose.
Place the brain into the mold with the ventral surface facing down.
Add more OCT if needed to completely submerge the brain in OCT.
Immediately place the mold on a level surface in the −80°C freezer for at least 24 hours prior to cryosectioning.
Incubate the embedded frozen brain at −20°C, either in a freezer or in the cryostat, for at least one hour before sectioning.
Place a fresh cryostat blade inside the cryostat and equilibrate its temperature to −20°C for at least 30 minutes prior to sectioning.
Mount the frozen brain to the specimen holder or chuck.
Cut the plastic mold from the embedded brain by removing the four corners with a razor or used cryostat blade.
Pour OCT medium on the pre-cooled chuck.
Place the embedded brain on the OCT before it freezes.
Allow the brain to freeze on the chuck for 10–20 minutes before sectioning.
Trim the excess OCT from the sides of the block with a razor or used cryostat blade.
Collect about 3–5 sections of the olfactory bulb and 8–10 sections of the forebrain, starting from the genu of the corpus callosum to the hippocampal commissure, on each slide.
Apply a drop of PBS on the slide with a brush immediately before collecting the section.
Use a gauze sponge dipped in PBS to remove unwanted tissue sections and OCT from the slide.
Equilibrate the frozen slides to room temperature for at least 15 min.
Place the slides in a moist chamber prepared with a paper towel soaked in distilled water in a tray.
Draw a line with a PAP pen along the periphery of the slide to form a hydrophobic barrier.
Wash the sections once with 500–800 μL 1× PBS for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Remove PBS either by tilting the slide to pour the liquid into the tray or aspirate the liquid with vacuum suction.
Attach a 200 μl pipet tip to the tip of the glass pipette attached to the suction tube for slowing the aspiration.
Add 500 μL of 0.5% PBS-Triton X-100 solution on each slide to permeabilize the tissue.
Incubate for 20 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Prepare the 1× Click-iT EdU buffer additive and use it to prepare the Click-iT Plus reaction cocktail.
Remove the PBS-Triton X-100 and wash the slide twice with 3% BSA-PBS solution.
Add 500 μL Click-iT Plus reaction cocktail to the slide and incubate for 30 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Protect from light by covering the transparent lid of the tray with aluminum foil.
Remove the Click-iT Plus reaction cocktail.
Wash once with 3% BSA-PBS solution for 5 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Remove the 3% BSA-PBS solution.
Wash three times with 500–800 μL of 1× PBS for 10 minutes each at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Fix the tissue with methanol by adding 500 μL of cold methanol on each slide.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Remove the methanol.
Wash the slide three times with 500–800 μL of 1× PBS per slide for 10 minutes/wash at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Add 500 μL of blocking buffer per slide.
Incubate for 45 minutes to 1 hour at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Remove the blocking solution.
Dilute the primary antibody in the BSA-Triton X100 solution to obtain the desired concentration.
Add 500 μL of diluted primary antibody per slide.
Incubate with the primary antibody for 2 hours at room temperature (20°C–25°C) or overnight at 4°C.
Remove the primary antibody after incubation.
Wash three times with 500–800 μL of 1× PBS per slide for 10 minutes/wash at room temperature.
Remove the PBS.
Add 500 μL of the secondary antibody with Hoechst stain per slide.
Incubate with the secondary antibody plus Hoechst for 1 hour at room temperature, protected from light.
Remove the secondary antibody.
Wash 3 times with 500–800 μL of 1× PBS per slide for 10 minutes/wash at room temperature.
Wash the slide once with 500–800 μL of distilled water per slide at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Mount coverslips with Fluoromount G mounting medium.
Gently aspirate the distilled water from around the tissue, taking care not to aspirate the tissue.
Dip a 500 μL pipet tip into Fluoromount G mounting medium and add 4–5 drops of the medium on each slide by touching the pipet tip to the slide.
Gently place the coverslip on the slide by hinging it from one end.
Allow Fluoromount G to solidify overnight or for 12–16 hours in the dark at room temperature before imaging.
